name: PixiEstim
description: An intelligent software project estimation platform that transforms heterogeneous project documents into structured, AI-assisted software estimations through controlled LLM workflows, historical RAG context, deterministic business rules, and human validation.
architectureCaption: Logical architecture of PixiEstim showing the separation between the frontend, business backend, persistence layer, asynchronous processing, document storage, and AI services.
problem: Software project estimation at PixiMind relied heavily on manually reading heterogeneous requirements documents, identifying functional requirements, selecting the appropriate estimation scales, evaluating implementation complexity, and consolidating effort estimates. The process could become time-consuming, difficult to standardize, and strongly dependent on the experience of the people involved, especially when documents were large, incomplete, or ambiguous.
solution: PixiEstim centralizes the software estimation workflow in a single platform. Project documents are uploaded and processed asynchronously, converted into structured and context-preserving segments, and analyzed through specialized AI workflows. The system proposes software features, associates validated features with internal estimation scales, evaluates their complexity, enriches decisions with similar historical cases through RAG, converts complexity levels into deterministic effort values, and keeps Sales and Production users in control through explicit human validation stages.
architecture: PixiEstim follows a distributed architecture composed of a Next.js frontend, a NestJS backend responsible for business logic, authorization, workflow coordination, and persistence, and a dedicated FastAPI service responsible for document processing and AI orchestration. PostgreSQL and Prisma manage structured business data. Redis and BullMQ support asynchronous processing, MinIO stores uploaded project documents, Qdrant stores and retrieves historical estimation knowledge through vector search, and Ollama provides local LLM inference. The application components are containerized with Docker and integrated into Jenkins-based CI/CD workflows.

aiEngineering.summary: PixiEstim implements a controlled AI workflow rather than delegating the full estimation process to a language model. Each intelligent stage has a specific responsibility, limited context, specialized prompt, expected structured output, application-level validation, fallback rules, traceability, and human validation where required.

pipeline.description: Project documents are uploaded, stored in MinIO, and submitted to an asynchronous processing workflow instead of being processed directly inside the request lifecycle.
FastAPI retrieves the document, detects its format, selects the appropriate extractor, and converts PDF, DOCX, or TXT content into a common internal representation.
Formatting noise and redundant visual information are removed while preserving section hierarchy, reading order, titles, paragraphs, lists, tables, and source provenance.
Large documents are divided along natural document boundaries into context-preserving segments compatible with the local model context window.
A specialized LLM call creates a global project context from the project name, main document sections, and relevant metadata before detailed feature extraction begins.
Document segments are processed progressively in batches. Each batch receives the global project context and previously extracted feature titles to preserve coherence and reduce duplication.
Generated outputs are parsed as JSON and validated against expected fields, formatting rules, closed candidate lists, and application-level constraints before persistence.
Generated feature titles are normalized and compared using a configurable similarity mechanism so strongly similar proposals can be consolidated before validation.
Generated features remain proposals. Authorized users can modify, remove, reorder, correct, or validate them, and only validated features can proceed to estimation.
Validated features are associated with one or more estimation scales selected for the current project. The model can only choose from the closed list of configured scales.
For each feature-scale pair, PixiEstim retrieves semantically similar historical estimation cases from Qdrant while applying metadata filtering and relevance controls.
The model evaluates each feature-scale pair using the current requirement, estimation scale, allowed complexity levels, and retrieved historical references.
The LLM does not generate arbitrary effort values. It selects a complexity level, and PixiEstim converts that level into effort using internally configured estimation values.
Production users review scale associations, complexity levels, calculated effort, fallback cases, and unassigned features before validating the final estimation.

promptEngineering.strategy: Task-specific prompts with constrained context, closed candidate sets, explicit rules, and structured outputs.

families.name: Project synthesis
families.purpose: Build a global project understanding before detailed analysis.

families.name: Feature extraction
families.purpose: Identify functional requirements from document segments.
families.output: Structured JSON list of software features

families.name: Scale association
families.purpose: Determine which configured technical estimation scales apply to each validated feature.
families.output: JSON associations restricted to authorized project scales

families.name: Complexity evaluation
families.purpose: Classify each feature-scale pair according to the allowed complexity scale.
families.output: One value from the predefined complexity levels

controls: Explicit model role for each AI task
Closed lists of authorized estimation scales
Previously extracted feature titles included during progressive extraction

rag.purpose: Ground complexity evaluation with comparable historical software estimation cases without treating historical decisions as automatic answers.
rag.knowledgeSource: Historical software estimation cases imported from Excel or CSV files.
rag.retrievalStrategy: The current feature and estimation context are converted into a query using the same embedding configuration used during indexing. Qdrant then performs semantic similarity search with estimation-scale filtering.
designDecisions: Historical complexity is stored as metadata but excluded from the semantic text used to build the search vector.
The same embedding configuration and preprocessing are used for indexing and retrieval.
References are filtered according to the relevant estimation scale before being added to the prompt.
Only references meeting the configured similarity threshold are retained.
Historical references are presented to the model as comparison cases rather than answers to reproduce.

guardrails.behavior: The response is rejected or retried before persistence.
An invalid element can be discarded while keeping the remaining usable output.
Strongly similar proposals are consolidated before human validation.
The association is rejected and the affected feature is flagged.

guardrails.control: Validation against the predefined five-level complexity scale
guardrails.behavior: A technical fallback is applied and the result is explicitly marked for human review.

guardrails.control: Metadata filtering using the estimation scale
guardrails.behavior: The reference is excluded before augmented-context construction.
The reference is not injected into the prompt and its absence remains traceable.
Only the highest-ranked historical references are retained.
The estimation continues without historical context and this execution mode is reported.

guardrails.risk: Blind reproduction of a historical estimate
guardrails.behavior: The model must reason from the current requirement and use historical cases only as comparison evidence.

humanInTheLoop.description: Human validation is used as a control mechanism at two critical stages of the AI workflow.

stages.description: Production or authorized users can edit, remove, reorder, deduplicate, and validate generated functional requirements. Only validated features enter the estimation pipeline.
Users review associated scales, complexity classifications, calculated effort, fallback values, and unassigned features before approving the final estimation.

observability.integration: Instrumentation is integrated around the FastAPI AI orchestration layer so a single execution can group observations from synthesis, extraction, scale association, RAG retrieval, and complexity evaluation.
observability.purpose: Support debugging, compare prompt variants, identify slow AI workflow stages, examine retrieval context, detect recurrent failures, and distinguish raw LLM output from data accepted by the application.

evaluation.status: Operational observability is implemented, while a formal offline retrieval-quality benchmark is not reported as a completed result.
recommendedOfflineMetrics: Exact complexity agreement with human validation

reliability: FastAPI isolates AI orchestration from the main NestJS business backend.
Each AI stage has one specialized responsibility instead of relying on a single monolithic prompt.
Structured LLM outputs are validated before persistence.
Asynchronous processing prevents long-running document operations from blocking normal application requests.
Intermediate workflow states and executions remain traceable.
Fallback values are visible and require verification instead of being silently accepted.
Only validated features can enter the estimation workflow.
Final AI-assisted estimations require human validation.
privacyAndCost: Local inference through Ollama reduces dependence on external LLM providers.
Keeping inference local provides greater control over confidential project documents.
Contextual segmentation avoids unnecessarily sending entire large documents to the model.
Local execution helps control operating costs while still consuming local compute resources.
Observability traces must limit unnecessary exposure of sensitive business information.

challenges: Processing heterogeneous and potentially large project documents without blocking the main application.
Preserving semantic structure and source context while converting PDF, DOCX, and TXT documents into AI-ready representations.
Adapting large documents to the limited context window of a locally hosted language model.
Extracting coherent software features progressively without losing the global project context.
Preventing malformed, incomplete, duplicated, or out-of-domain LLM outputs from entering the business workflow.
Associating generated features only with estimation scales authorized for the current project.
Retrieving relevant historical examples without introducing unrelated or overly influential references.
Keeping AI-generated recommendations under human control throughout feature generation and estimation.
Maintaining traceability across document processing, LLM calls, RAG retrieval, validation, fallback, and persistence stages.
Coordinating frontend, backend, AI services, PostgreSQL, Redis, BullMQ, MinIO, Qdrant, Ollama, and observability components within one workflow.
decisions: Separated AI and document-processing responsibilities into a dedicated FastAPI service while keeping business rules, authorization, and persistence inside NestJS.
Used Redis and BullMQ for asynchronous processing so document ingestion and AI workloads do not block the main application API.
Used MinIO object storage for uploaded project documents instead of storing binary files directly in PostgreSQL.
Used PostgreSQL and Prisma for structured business entities such as projects, users, clients, services, estimation scales, features, and estimation history.
Converted heterogeneous documents into a common internal representation before AI processing.
Used contextual segmentation based on natural document boundaries rather than fixed character-based chunking.
Used specialized prompts for project synthesis, feature extraction, scale association, and complexity evaluation instead of one general-purpose prompt.
Used structured JSON outputs and application-level validation around LLM responses.
Restricted estimation-scale associations and complexity classifications to closed lists of authorized values.
Used Qdrant to retrieve semantically similar historical estimation cases.
Excluded historical complexity from the embedded search text so the target value does not directly influence semantic similarity.
Applied scale-based filtering, Top-K retrieval, and a configurable similarity threshold before injecting historical context.
Converted AI-selected complexity levels into effort through deterministic business values instead of allowing the LLM to invent durations.
Introduced human validation between feature generation and estimation and again before final estimation approval.
Instrumented intelligent workflows through Langfuse to trace prompts, responses, retrieval context, durations, errors, and fallback behavior.
Used local inference through Ollama to improve control over confidentiality, external dependencies, and operating costs.
Containerized application services with Docker and automated build and deployment workflows through Jenkins.
results: Built an end-to-end workflow from project-document ingestion to validated software effort estimation.
Implemented asynchronous document ingestion and processing across NestJS, Redis, BullMQ, MinIO, and FastAPI.
Created a document-preparation pipeline covering extraction, normalization, structural reconstruction, contextual segmentation, persistence, and source traceability.
Implemented specialized LLM workflows for project synthesis, software-feature extraction, estimation-scale association, and complexity classification.
Added structured-output validation, deduplication, fallback handling, and business-rule enforcement around LLM responses.
Introduced human-in-the-loop validation before estimation and before final result approval.
Implemented deterministic conversion from AI-classified complexity to company-configured effort values.
Integrated historical estimation knowledge through a Qdrant-based RAG pipeline.
Implemented filtered semantic retrieval with Top-K = 2 and a configurable similarity threshold of 0.55.
Added RAG guardrails for domain filtering, low-relevance references, excessive context, missing references, and invalid complexity values.

Added observability for AI workflows through Langfuse, including model and prompt information, inputs, raw and validated outputs, durations, retrieval references, similarity scores, errors, and fallback behavior.
Containerized the frontend, backend, AI service, and supporting infrastructure and integrated them into Jenkins-based CI/CD workflows.

name: TejFlow
description: A business automation platform designed for accountants to retrieve, classify, archive, and manage Tunisian TEJ certificates while simplifying reporting and repetitive administrative workflows.
imageCaption: Illustrative mockup — not an actual production screenshot. Data and interface elements are fictionalized for portfolio presentation.
problem: Managing large numbers of TEJ certificates required accountants to perform repetitive administrative operations such as retrieving certificates, identifying their associated information, organizing documents, checking processing status, archiving records, and preparing data for reporting.
solution: TejFlow centralizes certificate-related workflows in a dedicated business application. It reduces repetitive operations by automating certificate retrieval and organization while providing accountants with structured views for classification, tracking, archiving, reporting, and day-to-day management.
architecture: TejFlow follows a client-server architecture with a React frontend and a Node.js/Express backend exposed through REST APIs. MongoDB stores certificate and workflow information, Zustand manages lightweight application state on the frontend, and Material UI provides reusable components for the business interface. Automation logic is implemented at the backend and integrated directly into the accountant workflow.
challenges: Transforming an existing manual accounting workflow into a structured digital process.
Automating repetitive certificate-management operations without making the workflow harder for accountants to understand.
Normalizing and classifying certificate information consistently.
Managing potentially large collections of certificates and their processing states.
Keeping client-side state synchronized after automated backend operations.
Designing an interface suitable for frequent use by non-technical business users.
decisions: Used React and Material UI to build a modular and business-oriented user interface.
Used Zustand instead of a heavier state-management solution to keep frontend state management simple.
Separated frontend and backend responsibilities through REST APIs.
Used MongoDB to support flexible certificate and workflow data structures.
Implemented automation directly around existing accounting operations rather than adding unnecessary AI complexity.
Designed certificate statuses and views around the real workflow followed by accountants.
results: Centralized certificate retrieval, classification, tracking, and archiving within one application.
Reduced repetitive manual operations involved in certificate management.
Improved visibility over the status and organization of certificate records.
Simplified access to information required for accounting and reporting workflows.
Built a reusable full-stack architecture focused on business process automation.

name: System Monitoring Application
description: A monitoring platform built with FastAPI to track endpoint availability, application performance metrics, and threshold violations through a centralized backend service.
problem: Applications and APIs require continuous visibility into endpoint availability and performance. Without centralized monitoring, failures, degraded response times, and threshold violations may remain unnoticed until they affect users.
solution: The application provides a centralized monitoring backend capable of performing endpoint health checks, tracking performance metrics, authenticating users, and generating alerts when monitored values exceed configured thresholds.
architecture: The backend is implemented with FastAPI and structured into routers, services, schemas, models, and core modules. MySQL stores monitoring data through SQLAlchemy, APScheduler executes scheduled monitoring operations, HTTPX performs HTTP requests against monitored endpoints, and Pydantic validates API data.
challenges: Running recurring endpoint checks without coupling scheduled tasks to API requests.
Recording monitoring metrics in a structured form suitable for later analysis.
Handling unavailable or slow endpoints without breaking the monitoring process.
Defining threshold-based alert conditions.
Separating API routes, business logic, validation, persistence, and monitoring services.
decisions: Used FastAPI to provide an asynchronous and strongly typed REST API.
Used APScheduler to execute recurring monitoring tasks.
Used HTTPX for HTTP health checks and monitored endpoint communication.
Used SQLAlchemy to separate persistence logic from the database implementation.
Used Pydantic schemas for request and response validation.
Structured the application into routers, services, models, schemas, and core modules.
results: Implemented real-time endpoint health monitoring.
Added performance metric tracking for monitored applications.
Implemented configurable alerts for threshold violations.
Added authentication and authorization around monitoring functionality.
Built a modular FastAPI backend that can be extended with additional monitoring capabilities.

name: Automatic License Plate Recognition
description: An AI-powered backend combining automatic license plate recognition, vehicle and violation management, and a RAG-based legal assistant for Tunisian traffic-law queries.
problem: Vehicle identification systems need to transform visual information into structured vehicle records while also giving operators efficient access to contextual information such as violations, payments, and applicable traffic regulations.
solution: The project combines an ALPR pipeline based on YOLOv8 and OCR with a FastAPI backend for vehicle dossiers and violations. It also integrates a RAG-powered legal assistant that retrieves traffic-law information and uses a Mistral language model to answer contextual legal questions. An agent mode can invoke application tools for more complex vehicle-related queries.
architecture: FastAPI exposes the ALPR, vehicle, chat, and agent APIs. Images are processed through a YOLOv8-based plate detection pipeline followed by OCR and plate normalization. MongoDB stores vehicle, violation, and payment data. Legal documents are indexed into a FAISS vector index for retrieval, while Mistral generates answers based on the retrieved context. Repository and service layers isolate persistence and business logic.
challenges: Detecting license plates from images under varying image conditions.
Converting OCR output into normalized and usable license plate identifiers.
Connecting recognition results with persistent vehicle and violation records.
Retrieving relevant traffic-law passages for legal questions.
Combining vehicle context with RAG-based legal responses.
Exposing AI and computer-vision operations through clean backend APIs.
Supporting both conversational questions and tool-driven agent operations.
decisions: Used YOLOv8 for license plate detection and segmentation.
Separated plate detection, OCR, and normalization into dedicated ALPR modules.
Used MongoDB for vehicle, violation, and payment documents.
Used FastAPI to expose recognition and AI functionality through REST endpoints.
Used FAISS to index and retrieve relevant traffic-law documents.
Integrated Mistral for language-model responses based on retrieved legal context.
Created a separate agent endpoint capable of using application tools for structured operations.
Separated API routes, repositories, services, schemas, RAG logic, and LLM integration into distinct modules.
results: Built a complete backend pipeline from uploaded vehicle image to recognized plate.
Connected recognized plates with vehicle, violation, and payment information.
Added a RAG-powered assistant for questions related to Tunisian traffic regulations.
Implemented contextual legal queries using both retrieved documents and vehicle information.
Added an agent mode for tool-based operations.
Designed the backend so computer vision, persistence, RAG, and LLM components remain independently maintainable.

name: Digi School
description: A school management system built around a Laravel backend with secure authentication, background jobs, testing, and a responsive web interface.
problem: Educational institutions need centralized applications for managing school-related information and operations instead of relying on fragmented manual processes and disconnected tools.
solution: Digi School provides a centralized school-management application with authenticated access, API-based functionality, responsive interfaces, background processing, and a backend architecture designed around Laravel conventions.
architecture: The application uses Laravel 11 and PHP for backend and application logic, JWT and Laravel Sanctum for authentication, Tailwind CSS for the interface, Vite for frontend asset bundling, and Laravel queues for background tasks. Pest PHP is used for automated testing.
challenges: Structuring a school-management domain containing multiple related business entities.
Protecting application functionality through authentication and authorization.
Separating synchronous user operations from background processing.
Providing a responsive interface suitable for different screen sizes.
Keeping application behavior testable while the domain grows.
decisions: Used Laravel to benefit from its structured MVC ecosystem and built-in application services.
Used JWT and Laravel Sanctum for secure authentication.
Used Laravel queues for operations that can be processed outside the main request lifecycle.
Used Tailwind CSS to build a responsive interface.
Used Pest PHP to introduce automated testing.
Used Vite for frontend asset development and bundling.
results: Built a structured application foundation for school-management workflows.
Implemented secure authentication and protected application functionality.
Added background job processing through Laravel queues.
Created a responsive web interface.
Added automated tests using Pest PHP.

name: Bid TUN
description: A full-stack auction platform allowing users to create and manage auctions, place bids, receive live notifications, and track auction activity in real time.
problem: Online auctions require multiple users to interact with the same listings while bids, auction states, and notifications change continuously. Traditional request-response interfaces can provide outdated information during active auctions.
solution: Bid TUN provides a full-stack auction experience where authenticated users can create listings, manage profiles, place bids, follow active auctions, receive live notifications, and visualize auction-related information.
architecture: The frontend is built with React, Chakra UI, Redux Toolkit, React Router, and Axios. Laravel provides the backend API with Laravel Sanctum for authentication and MySQL for persistence. Pusher and Laravel Echo provide real-time WebSocket communication for bid and notification updates. Docker configuration supports containerized deployment.
challenges: Keeping auction state synchronized across multiple connected users.
Delivering bid and notification updates without requiring manual page refreshes.
Managing authenticated frontend and backend communication.
Maintaining predictable application state across listings, bids, profiles, and notifications.
Designing responsive auction interfaces around rapidly changing data.
decisions: Used React for a component-based interactive frontend.
Used Redux Toolkit for centralized client-side application state.
Used Laravel and MySQL for backend business logic and persistence.
Used Laravel Sanctum for authenticated API access.
Integrated Pusher and Laravel Echo for WebSocket-based real-time updates.
Used Chakra UI to create reusable responsive interface components.
Added Docker configuration to simplify application packaging and deployment.
results: Implemented auction creation and management.
Built a real-time bidding workflow.
Added live notifications through WebSockets.
Implemented secure user authentication and profile management.
Added auction analytics and responsive listing interfaces.
Containerized the frontend for reproducible deployment.

name: Medical Appointment Platform
description: A responsive healthcare application connecting patients with healthcare providers through doctor discovery, appointment scheduling, notifications, and administrative interfaces.
problem: Patients need an accessible way to discover healthcare providers and organize medical appointments, while administrators require interfaces for managing platform information and services.
solution: FindDoctor provides a React-based healthcare interface with authenticated access, advanced doctor search, appointment scheduling, notifications, administrative views, and integration with a dedicated backend API.
architecture: The frontend is built with React 18 and Vite. React Router handles client-side navigation, Axios provides backend API communication, and Tailwind CSS handles responsive styling. The application separates pages, reusable components, context providers, and API services into dedicated modules.
challenges: Designing appointment workflows that remain easy to understand for patients.
Organizing doctor search and healthcare information within a responsive interface.
Managing authentication state throughout the application.
Handling API loading states, failures, and user feedback consistently.
Supporting both patient-facing interfaces and administrative functionality.
decisions: Used React to build reusable user-interface components.
Used Vite for a lightweight frontend development environment.
Separated external API communication into dedicated service modules.
Used React context for application-level state.
Used Tailwind CSS for responsive styling.
Added toast notifications, loading states, and error handling to improve user feedback.
results: Built doctor discovery and advanced search interfaces.
Implemented appointment-scheduling workflows.
Integrated authentication and authorization with the backend API.
Added real-time user notifications and feedback states.
Created responsive interfaces for both users and administrators.

name: QuizMaster Pro
description: A multilingual Flutter quiz application combining Firebase services, persistent score tracking, push notifications, localization, theming, and interactive user feedback.
problem: Quiz applications need more than static questions to maintain user engagement. Users expect persistent progress, immediate feedback, multilingual support, notifications, personalization, and a consistent experience across devices.
solution: QuizMaster Pro delivers an interactive cross-platform quiz experience with authenticated and anonymous usage, score history, countdown timers, sound and visual feedback, multilingual interfaces, light and dark themes, push notifications, and local persistence.
architecture: The application is built with Flutter and Dart using Riverpod for state management. Firebase Authentication manages user identities, Cloud Firestore stores score history, Firebase Cloud Messaging provides push notifications, and SharedPreferences stores lightweight local preferences. The codebase separates controllers, models, screens, services, localization resources, and reusable widgets.
challenges: Synchronizing quiz state, timers, scoring, and user interactions.
Supporting authenticated and anonymous users.
Providing localization across English, French, and Arabic.
Persisting score history remotely while retaining local application preferences.
Handling push and local notifications across mobile application states.
Maintaining responsive layouts across different screen sizes.
decisions: Used Flutter to maintain a single cross-platform mobile codebase.
Used Riverpod for predictable application state management.
Used Firebase Authentication for both email/password and anonymous authentication.
Used Cloud Firestore to persist score history.
Used Firebase Cloud Messaging together with local notifications for user engagement.
Used SharedPreferences for lightweight local persistence.
Separated localization files from application logic to support multiple languages cleanly.
results: Implemented multilingual support for English, French, and Arabic.
Added persistent score history using Firestore.
Implemented push and local notifications.
Added light and dark theme support.
Implemented timers, sound feedback, and visual celebration effects.
Structured the application into reusable controllers, services, models, screens, and widgets.
